steps.intent: Our objectives are to renew cross-border humanitarian access in a limited and temporary manner that respects Syrian sovereignty, reduces the authorized crossings to two, and prioritizes cross-line deliveries with the consent of the Syrian authorities while strengthening counter-terrorism safeguards. We expect difficult negotiations with Western members over the number of crossings, the duration of the renewal, and language on coordination with the Syrian Government. We also anticipate concerns from humanitarian actors about reduced access, but we believe this balanced compromise can secure the necessary votes and avoid a veto.

messages.Belgium: Belgium supports renewal of the cross-border mechanism, but the current text falls short on duration and access. We need a twelve-month renewal that retains the existing four crossings, including Al Yarubiyah, and we cannot accept language that makes cross-line delivery conditional on the Syrian authorities' consent. Any counter-diversion measures must not impede principled humanitarian access.
messages.China: China supports the Russian draft as a balanced and realistic basis. It reflects the temporary and exceptional nature of the cross-border mechanism, respect for Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity, the primary responsibility of the Syrian authorities, and the need to combat terrorism and prevent diversion of humanitarian assistance. We urge Council members to support the text and avoid politicizing humanitarian assistance.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d'Ivoire supports renewing the cross-border mechanism and thanks the Russian Federation for circulating a draft. However, we are concerned that limiting the mandate to six months and two crossings may leave civilians in need without adequate assistance. We therefore ask that the renewal cover all four currently authorized crossings, particularly Al-Yarubiyah, and be extended for twelve months, with clear reporting on humanitarian impact. We also seek language ensuring that monitoring does not impede humanitarian deliveries and that cross-line efforts do not make cross-border assistance conditional.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic welcomes the renewal of the cross-border mechanism and supports keeping Bab al-Hawa and Bab al-Salam operational. However, six months is insufficient for predictable humanitarian planning; we ask for a twelve-month renewal. We cannot accept language that conditions cross-line deliveries on the consent of the Syrian authorities, as this undermines humanitarian principles. We also ask that coordination and monitoring language not create new impediments to access.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the draft as a basis for renewing the cross-border mechanism. We believe it is important to maintain Council unity and to ensure that humanitarian assistance continues to reach all parts of Syria without interruption. We call on all members to work constructively and in good faith to renew the mechanism before its expiration.
messages.France: France supports renewing the cross-border mechanism but cannot accept a six-month renewal limited to two crossings. We ask the penholder to restore a twelve-month mandate and the three crossings currently authorized, including Al Yarubiyah. France remains ready to work constructively for a balanced text that preserves humanitarian access to all Syrians.
messages.Germany: Germany cannot support the current text, which would cut off lifesaving cross-border assistance to millions of civilians. Our red line is the retention of all four existing crossings; we also insist on a 12-month renewal and on removing language that conditions cross-line deliveries on the consent of the Syrian authorities. These changes are essential for Germany to support the renewal.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia supports renewal of the cross-border mechanism to save lives, but a six-month mandate limited to two crossings risks disrupting essential humanitarian access, particularly to northeast Syria. We therefore ask the penholder to extend the mandate to twelve months and retain all four crossings. We also seek language ensuring cross-line deliveries are conducted in line with humanitarian principles and reach all people in need without discrimination.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait supports the renewal of the cross-border mechanism, but we cannot accept a text that reduces access to populations in need or conditions humanitarian action on the consent of the Syrian authorities. We ask the penholder to retain the Al Yarubiyah crossing, extend the authorization for twelve months, and align OP3 and OP5 with humanitarian principles. Kuwait remains ready to work constructively toward a consensus text that preserves life-saving assistance.
messages.Peru: Peru supports renewal of the cross-border mechanism, which remains indispensable for reaching civilians in need. We cannot accept a reduction to only two crossings, and we ask that all four existing crossings be retained and the renewal be predictable. We also seek safeguards so that cross-line efforts do not condition or weaken the cross-border mechanism, and stronger reporting on access constraints.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot accept the reduction of authorized crossings or the six-month duration. We ask that OP1 renew the mechanism for twelve months and retain all four crossings, and that OP5 not condition cross-line deliveries on the consent of the Syrian authorities. We support robust monitoring against diversion, but it must not become a pretext to restrict humanitarian access.
messages.South Africa: South Africa supports the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism, as the humanitarian situation remains dire. We ask the penholder to extend the mandate to twelve months for predictability and to ensure the mechanism can reach all areas of need, including through the other authorized crossings where needs persist. We also seek language ensuring that access is not unduly restricted and remains in line with humanitarian principles, while respecting Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support this text as drafted. We support renewal of the cross-border mechanism, but the removal of Al Yarubiyah would cut a lifeline for millions of people in northeast Syria and shortening the mandate to six months would undermine the predictability of humanitarian operations. We call for a twelve-month renewal and the retention of all three crossings, and we will not support a text that closes Al Yarubiyah.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft as written. We need a 12-month renewal and retention of all three existing crossings, including Al Yarubiyah, to match humanitarian needs. We also oppose language subjecting cross-border delivery to Syrian authorities' consent or suggesting that the regime bears primary responsibility for humanitarian access. These are red lines, but we are ready to work in good faith on a viable text.

steps.summary: The revised text preserves the six-month renewal and two crossings while adding monitoring safeguards, an oral briefing, and 'without undue restrictions' language to address humanitarian concerns. We expect 11 votes in favour and 4 abstentions, with no P5 veto.
diff: The Security Council, Recalling its resolutions 2042 (2012), 2043 (2012), 2118 (2013), … its humanitarian partners to deliver humanitarian assistance to all parts of Syria,
including through cross-line deliveries, and encouraging further efforts to expand these deliveries with the consent of the Syrian authorities,
1. Decides that the authorization and modalities set out in paragraphs 2 … this resolution, including on the humanitarian situation, the use of the crossings,
any impediments to the delivery of humanitarian assistance,
the impact of the reduction in the number of authorized crossings,
recommendations on how to improve cross-line

deliveries and address any resulting humanitarian gaps, within 60 days; and further requests the Secretary-General to provide an oral briefing to the Council within 30 days on the humanitarian situation;
3. Emphasizes that the delivery of humanitarian assistance must be in accordance with the humanitarian principles and in coordination with the relevant parties,
including the Syrian authorities and United Nations humanitarian agencies and their implementing partners,
and that all parties must ensure unhindered
access and that assistance reaches all people in need without discrimination;
4. Calls upon all parties to ensure the safety and security of … intensify efforts to expand cross-line deliveries with the consent of the Syrian
authorities and without undue restrictions, in accordance with humanitarian principles and international humanitarian law;
6. Stresses the need to strengthen the monitoring and reporting mechanism to … Secretary-General to include in his report information on measures taken in this
regard, and that such monitoring and reporting shall be consistent with humanitarian principles and shall not impede or delay the delivery of humanitarian assistance;
7. Decides to remain actively seized of the matter.

messages.Belgium: We welcome the OP6 safeguard, but the core humanitarian access issues remain unresolved. Belgium cannot support a text that reduces authorized crossings to two, conditions cross-line deliveries on Syrian consent, and shortens the mandate to six months. Unless OP1 restores the four crossings and OP5 removes the consent requirement, we will not be able to vote in favour.
messages.China: China supports the revised draft as a balanced basis for renewing the humanitarian cross-border mechanism. We welcome its reaffirmation of Syria’s sovereignty and the primary responsibility of the Syrian authorities, its recognition that the cross-border mechanism is temporary, and its emphasis on expanding cross-line deliveries and preventing diversion to terrorist groups. China calls on all Council members to support the text and avoid politicization of humanitarian assistance.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d'Ivoire thanks the penholder for incorporating the OP6 safeguard on monitoring and reporting. While we would have preferred a longer renewal and the retention of all four border crossings, we recognize the current text as a compromise that preserves essential humanitarian access and Council unity. We therefore support the draft as it stands.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic welcomes the acceptance of our OP3 and OP6 safeguards, but our red line on OP5 remains: humanitarian access should not be made conditional on the consent of the Syrian authorities, and cross-line deliveries must be carried out in cooperation with all relevant parties and in accordance with humanitarian principles. We also continue to believe that a six-month renewal is too short and that a twelve-month renewal would provide the predictability needed by humanitarian partners. We urge the penholder to show flexibility on these points so that the Council can speak clearly on the humanitarian situation.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: We thank the Russian Federation for the revised draft. Equatorial Guinea supports this text as a balanced compromise that reaffirms Syria's sovereignty while preserving humanitarian access through the authorized crossings and strengthening monitoring against diversion. We call on all Council members to show flexibility and unity so that the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people are not held hostage to geopolitical differences.
messages.France: France cannot support the text as currently drafted. We maintain that the Al Yarubiyah crossing must be included, as it is essential for humanitarian access to northeast Syria, and we seek a 12-month renewal for predictability. Without these changes, France will abstain.
messages.Germany: Germany appreciates the penholder's efforts, but the current text does not yet meet the humanitarian minimum. Cutting the authorization to two crossings for six months, while inserting language requiring Syrian consent, risks denying principled access to millions in need. As a minimum, we need Al-Yarubiyah restored and the consent language removed; we also continue to call for a twelve-month renewal. Germany is ready to support a balanced text that preserves effective cross-border access.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia supports the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism, which remains a lifeline for millions of Syrians. We appreciate the penholder’s partial acceptance of our earlier proposals, including the added non-discrimination and UN agency language. However, we continue to believe that a six-month renewal and only two crossings will leave serious humanitarian gaps, especially in the northeast and for populations reliant on Al Yarubiyah and Al Ramtha. We therefore urge the penholder to extend the authorization to twelve months and retain all four crossings so that assistance reaches all people in need without discrimination.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait appreciates the partial acceptance on OP3 and remains committed to a unified Council renewal. However, the removal of Al Yarubiyah is a red line: it provides essential access to northeast Syria and must be restored. We can accept the six-month duration and other language, but we cannot support the draft without Al Yarubiyah.
messages.Peru: Peru cannot support the current text because it reduces the authorized border crossings to two and conditions cross-line deliveries on Syrian authorities' consent, which risks further restricting humanitarian access to civilians in need. We reiterate our red line that Al-Ramtha and Al-Yarubiyah must remain authorized, and we urge the penholder to restore all four crossings and remove the consent requirement. Peru remains committed to a balanced renewal that upholds humanitarian principles and ensures unimpeded access to all parts of Syria.
messages.Poland: Poland welcomes the OP6 safeguard and can support renewal to prevent a humanitarian gap. We continue to ask that the mandate be restored to twelve months and cover Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam, Al Yarubiyah and Al Ramtha, given the needs across Syria. We also ask that OP5 not make humanitarian access conditional on the consent of the Syrian authorities, but instead reaffirm principled and unimpeded access. Poland will not block lifesaving assistance, but these changes remain important for our support.
messages.South Africa: South Africa supports the renewal of the cross-border mechanism as a necessary humanitarian measure to prevent further suffering. We welcome the addition of 'without undue restrictions' in OP5 and the reporting requirements in OP2, which allow the Council to assess the impact of reducing the number of authorized crossings. While we would have preferred a longer renewal and the retention of Al Yarubiyah and Al Ramtha, we do not wish to block this draft and will support it, urging all parties to facilitate unimpeded humanitarian access.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: We regret that the penholder has not accommodated our red line. The UK cannot support a text that eliminates Al Yarubiyah, which is a lifeline for medical supplies to northeast Syria. We also continue to believe a 12-month renewal is necessary to provide predictability. We urge the penholder to restore the third crossing and extend the mandate.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support a text that cuts off the Al Yarubiyah crossing, which is a lifeline for civilians in northeast Syria, or that conditions cross-line aid on the consent of the Syrian authorities. We can accept a six-month renewal if Al Yarubiyah is retained and OP5 is revised to remove the consent requirement and ensure aid is delivered in accordance with humanitarian principles. We also continue to support a 12-month renewal for predictability, but the crossings and consent language are our red lines. Without these changes, we will be unable to support the resolution.

reasons.Belgium: Belgium’s key red lines—restoring the four crossings and deleting the consent language in OP5—were not accepted, and its last-round position was to oppose. The final text therefore does not meet Belgium’s humanitarian-access requirements.
reasons.China: China’s position aligns with the Russian draft’s emphasis on Syrian sovereignty, consent-based humanitarian delivery, counterterrorism safeguards, and cross-line expansion; China supported the draft in negotiations and requested no changes.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire indicated support for the draft in the last negotiation round and has consistently backed humanitarian renewals. The draft’s 12-month extension of cross-border assistance aligns with its humanitarian priorities, so it votes in favour.
reasons.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic’s OP5 red line—removing the consent requirement of the Syrian authorities—was not met, and its prior record shows opposition to comparable Russian counter-drafts on humanitarian access. Voting against is consistent with its stated commitment to humanitarian principles and unconditional access.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supported the Russian draft in the last negotiation round and made no requests for changes; the text’s emphasis on Syrian sovereignty, humanitarian access, and Council action aligns with its stated priorities.
reasons.France: France’s key requests—three crossings including Al Yarubiyah and a twelve-month renewal—were accepted, aligning with its priority to preserve cross-border humanitarian access. Despite remaining concerns, France supports the draft as a workable compromise.
reasons.Germany: Germany’s red line on retaining Al Yarubiyah and its important request for a twelve-month renewal were accepted, while the remaining rejected changes were important but not red lines. Maintaining the cross-border mechanism is essential for Germany’s humanitarian priorities, so it votes in favour while flagging concerns.
reasons.Indonesia: Indonesia abstained because its key request to retain the Al Ramtha crossing was not accepted, even though the 12-month renewal was granted. It did not speak before the vote, consistent with its practice of making post-vote statements.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait’s requested red line—restoring Al Yarubiyah—was accepted by the penholder, and Kuwait’s established position supports humanitarian cross-border access as a temporary measure while emphasizing Syrian sovereignty and non-diversion. It therefore votes in favour and explains its vote before the vote.
reasons.Peru: Peru had declared maintaining all four cross-border crossings a red line and had already opposed the draft; because Al-Ramtha is omitted and the problematic consent language remains, Peru maintains its opposition.
reasons.Poland: Poland had pressed for all four crossings and deletion of consent language, and its record shows it opposed similar Russian drafts that weakened humanitarian access; the partial acceptance of a 12-month renewal did not satisfy its core humanitarian concerns.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the sponsor and a permanent member committed to Syrian sovereignty and a balanced humanitarian mechanism, Russia will vote in favour and explain its position. The draft reflects Russian priorities: a temporary mechanism, Syrian consent, cross-line expansion and counterterrorism safeguards.
reasons.South Africa: South Africa’s prior positions show support for renewing cross-border humanitarian access while stressing Syrian sovereignty and avoiding politicization; it was recorded as supporting this draft in the last negotiation round.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK had opposed the Russian draft in negotiations and, despite the inclusion of Al Yarubiyah and a 12-month renewal, the text retained problematic language subordinating cross-border aid to Syrian government consent; the UK would instead support the humanitarian penholders' draft.
reasons.United States of America: The draft meets the United States’ core objectives of a twelve-month renewal and preserving the three crossings; a lapse in lifesaving cross-border aid would be far worse than the retained OP5 language, which concerns cross-line deliveries and can be addressed through implementation and reporting. The US therefore votes in favour while flagging concerns about regime consent.

before.Belgium: Mr. President, Belgium remains fully committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and to the delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance to all Syrians in need. We support the renewal of the cross-border mechanism as an indispensable lifeline. However, the text before us does not meet the humanitarian requirements we have consistently set out. It fails to authorize all the crossings needed, including Al Ramtha, and it retains in paragraph 5 a consent requirement that risks subordinating principled cross-line humanitarian access to political considerations. While we welcome the extension to twelve months, these shortcomings mean that Belgium cannot support this draft. We will vote against it.
before.China: China thanks the Russian Federation for its efforts to advance a balanced draft. We support the renewal of the cross-border mechanism as a temporary measure, while stressing that Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity must be fully respected. Humanitarian assistance must be delivered in accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, with the consent of the Syrian authorities, and we must also prevent any diversion of assistance to terrorist groups and work to expand cross-line deliveries. China will vote in favour.
before.Côte d’Ivoire: Thank you, Mr. President. Côte d’Ivoire will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We remain deeply concerned by the humanitarian situation in Syria and believe that renewing the cross-border mechanism is essential to ensure that humanitarian assistance reaches all civilians in need. We welcome the reaffirmation of the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, as well as the emphasis on the protection of civilians. At the same time, we stress that humanitarian access must not be obstructed and call on all parties to facilitate the rapid, safe and unhindered delivery of assistance to all parts of Syria, in accordance with international humanitarian law. Côte d’Ivoire hopes that the Council will continue to seek consensus and a unified approach to alleviate the suffering of the Syrian people.
before.Dominican Republic: Thank you, Mr. President. The Dominican Republic strongly supports the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism and appreciates the extension of the authorization for twelve months. We also recognize the urgent need for humanitarian assistance to reach all civilians in Syria. However, we cannot support a text that retains the requirement of consent by the Syrian authorities for the expansion of cross-line deliveries. Humanitarian access must be governed by humanitarian principles and international humanitarian law, not by the consent of any party to the conflict. The Dominican Republic will therefore vote against the draft resolution.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism for twelve months and the retention of the three crossings, including Al Yarubiyah, which remain essential to reaching civilians in need. France reiterates that humanitarian assistance must be delivered in full respect of humanitarian principles, and that cross-line deliveries, while important, cannot substitute for cross-border operations. We call on all parties to ensure safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access throughout Syria.
before.Germany: Germany will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism for twelve months and the retention of the three crossings, including Al Yarubiyah, which are indispensable for reaching millions of civilians in need. At the same time, we regret that our proposed amendments to paragraphs 3 and 5 were not taken up. We stress that humanitarian assistance must be delivered in accordance with humanitarian principles through United Nations humanitarian actors and partners, and that cross-border operations must not be subordinated to the consent of the Syrian authorities. We will vote in favour because the renewal is urgently needed, but we will continue to insist on full respect for humanitarian principles and on effective monitoring without impeding humanitarian action.
before.Kuwait: Mr. President, the State of Kuwait will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome the inclusion of the Al Yarubiyah crossing, which is essential for reaching civilians in north-eastern Syria and was a red line for my delegation. We support renewing the cross-border mechanism as a temporary, life-saving measure, in accordance with humanitarian principles and in full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity. We stress that humanitarian assistance must not be politicized or diverted, that all parties must ensure unhindered access, and that cross-line deliveries must be expanded. Kuwait remains committed to a political solution consistent with resolution 2254 (2015).
before.Peru: Peru will vote against this draft resolution. We appreciate that the renewal period has been extended to 12 months, but the text does not meet the fundamental humanitarian requirements that we have consistently set out. In particular, it reduces the number of authorized border crossings by omitting Al-Ramtha, despite the clear need to preserve all four crossings so that humanitarian assistance can reach all people in need throughout Syria. Peru cannot support a text that risks narrowing humanitarian access and that does not fully safeguard the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. We remain committed to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, and we will continue to support every effort to ensure that humanitarian relief reaches civilians without discrimination and without undue restrictions.
before.Poland: Poland fully supports the renewal of the Security Council’s cross-border humanitarian mechanism and welcomes the acceptance of a twelve-month period. At the same time, we regret that the draft before us does not preserve all four authorized crossings and retains language that makes cross-line deliveries subject to the consent of the Syrian authorities. Humanitarian access must be needs-based and consistent with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence; it cannot be conditional in a manner that risks denying life-saving assistance to civilians in need. Poland therefore cannot support this draft and will vote against it.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation has consistently held that humanitarian assistance to Syria must be delivered in full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the country. The draft before the Council is a balanced text. It renews the cross-border mechanism for twelve months, while reaffirming that this mechanism is temporary and that the primary responsibility for assisting the Syrian people lies with the Syrian authorities. It also calls for expanding cross-line deliveries with the consent of the Syrian authorities and strengthens measures to prevent the diversion of humanitarian aid to terrorist groups, without politicizing humanitarian work. We believe the draft responds to the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people and respects the fundamental principles of international humanitarian law. The Russian Federation will vote in favour and calls on all members to support it.
before.South Africa: South Africa remains gravely concerned by the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Syria and the suffering of civilians, including those in areas that depend on cross-border assistance. We believe that the renewal of the cross-border mechanism is necessary to ensure that lifesaving humanitarian assistance continues to reach all people in need, in accordance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. At the same time, South Africa reaffirms its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria. The cross-border mechanism is a temporary measure, and we encourage the United Nations and all parties to expand cross-line deliveries with the consent of the Syrian authorities and without undue restrictions. Humanitarian assistance must never be politicized or used as an instrument of pressure, and counter-terrorism measures must not impede the delivery of aid to civilians. South Africa also reiterates the need for a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process in line with resolution 2254 (2015). It is on that basis that South Africa will vote in favour of the draft resolution before us.
before.United States of America: The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. We do so because it renews the Council’s cross-border authorization for twelve months and preserves the three crossings of Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al Yarubiyah, which are lifelines for millions of Syrians in need. We welcome the acceptance of Al Yarubiyah and the twelve-month duration. At the same time, we remain concerned that language in the draft could be read as subjecting humanitarian access to the consent of the Syrian regime. We stress that the Council’s cross-border authorization is not subject to the approval of the Assad regime, and that all parties must allow rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We expect the Secretary-General to report clearly on implementation, including efforts to expand cross-line deliveries without undue restrictions, and on measures to prevent the diversion of assistance to terrorist groups. The United States will continue to stand with the Syrian people and to pursue accountability for the regime’s atrocities.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China regrets that the draft resolution on the humanitarian situation in Syria was not adopted. China voted in favour because the text provided for the renewal of the cross-border mechanism as a temporary measure and, at the same time, reaffirmed Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and the primary responsibility of the Syrian authorities for the delivery of humanitarian assistance.

The humanitarian situation in Syria is grave and complicated. Humanitarian assistance must be delivered in strict accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, with the consent of the Syrian authorities, and must reach all people in need without discrimination. At the same time, the Council must pay attention to the risk of diversion of humanitarian supplies to terrorist groups. The cross-border mechanism is temporary; cross-line deliveries with the consent of the Syrian authorities should be expanded.

China has consistently opposed politicizing humanitarian issues. The failure of the Council to adopt this draft does not serve the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people. We call on all parties to engage in constructive consultations, take into account the reasonable concerns of all sides, and work toward a balanced and viable arrangement that truly benefits the Syrian people.
after.Côte d’Ivoire: Thank you, Mr. President. Côte d’Ivoire takes the floor to express its deep regret that the draft resolution before the Council was not adopted, despite our vote in favour. The humanitarian situation in Syria remains grave, and the cross-border mechanism is a lifeline for millions of civilians. My delegation supported the renewal because we believe the Council must not leave a humanitarian vacuum. At the same time, we have listened carefully to the concerns expressed by other members, including on the need to preserve all necessary crossings and to ensure that humanitarian access is governed by humanitarian principles and not obstructed by any party. Côte d’Ivoire calls on all members of the Council to resume dialogue in a spirit of compromise and to find a consensus solution before the current authorization expires. The protection of civilians and the delivery of impartial, neutral and independent humanitarian assistance must remain our common priority. We stand ready to work with all delegations to that end.
after.Equatorial Guinea:
Mr. President, Equatorial Guinea voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation because it would have renewed for twelve months the cross-border humanitarian mechanism, which remains a vital lifeline for millions of Syrian civilians, and because it preserved the three crossings of Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al Yarubiyah. The text was not perfect, but the humanitarian situation in Syria is grave, and the Council could not afford a vacuum or an interruption in the delivery of life-saving assistance.

We deeply regret that this draft was not adopted. Once again, the Security Council has been unable to speak with one voice on a matter involving the lives of civilians — women, children, the sick, the displaced and people with special needs. Equatorial Guinea continues to believe that humanitarian assistance must never be politicized and must be delivered in accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence.

At the same time, we stress that the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria must be fully respected. The cross-border mechanism is a temporary measure and must not replace cross-line deliveries, which should be expanded with the consent of the Syrian authorities and without undue restrictions. We call on all parties to ensure safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access and to protect humanitarian personnel. We urge the Council to continue negotiations in a spirit of flexibility and unity so that a consensus can be reached before the expiration of the mechanism. Equatorial Guinea remains ready to engage constructively to that end.
after.Germany: Thank you, Mr. President. Germany deeply regrets that the Security Council has again failed to adopt a renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism. We voted in favour of this draft because a twelve-month renewal, preserving the three crossings of Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al Yarubiyah, would have helped ensure that life-saving assistance continues to reach millions of Syrians in need. The humanitarian situation remains grave, and the Council cannot allow humanitarian access to become a casualty of political division. We continue to believe that humanitarian assistance must be delivered in full accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence, and that cross-border operations must not be subordinated to the consent of the Syrian authorities. At the same time, a failure to renew the mechanism would be worse for civilians. Germany urges all Council members to work urgently and constructively before the current authorization expires so that the Council can adopt a principled, predictable and needs-based renewal that preserves cross-border access and supports expanded cross-line deliveries in line with international humanitarian law. The humanitarian imperative must prevail.
after.Indonesia:
Mr. President,

Indonesia abstained on the draft resolution before the Council. We did so after careful consideration and with a strong sense of the humanitarian imperative in Syria.

Indonesia supports the renewal of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism as a temporary, life-saving measure. We recognize the importance of the Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al Yarubiyah crossings, and we welcome the twelve-month extension, as well as the emphasis on expanding cross-line deliveries, respecting Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and preventing the diversion of humanitarian assistance to terrorist groups.

At the same time, we remain concerned that the text does not fully reflect the humanitarian principles and does not adequately preserve needs-based humanitarian access. In particular, the question of all authorized crossings and the consent requirement in paragraph 5 require a more balanced and consensus-based approach. For these reasons, Indonesia could not vote in favour.

Indonesia did not vote against the draft because the delivery of humanitarian assistance to millions of Syrians must not be held hostage to political differences. We regret that the Council has again not been able to speak with one voice. We call on all members to put people first, to preserve the unity of the Council, and to continue working towards a principled, balanced and consensus-based solution that ensures rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all people in need throughout Syria, in accordance with international humanitarian law and the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence.

Indonesia remains committed to a political solution consistent with resolution 2254 (2015).
after.Kuwait:
Mr. President,

The State of Kuwait regrets that the Security Council has not been able to adopt the draft resolution before it. We voted in favour because the text renewed the cross-border humanitarian mechanism for twelve months and, importantly, retained the Al Yarubiyah crossing. For Kuwait, that crossing is not a technical detail; it is a humanitarian lifeline for civilians in north-eastern Syria, and its absence would deepen an already catastrophic situation.

At the same time, we reaffirm that the cross-border mechanism is a temporary and exceptional measure. It must be implemented in full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and in strict accordance with the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. Humanitarian assistance must not be politicized or diverted to terrorist groups. All parties must facilitate safe, rapid and unhindered access to all people in need, and cross-line deliveries must be expanded.

The Council’s inability to act today should not become a sentence of further suffering for the Syrian people. We call on all members to continue engaging in good faith and to find a practical arrangement before the current authorization expires. Kuwait remains ready to work with all members and with the United Nations to ensure that life-saving assistance reaches all Syrians, and we reiterate the need for a political solution consistent with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva communiqué.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution that it submitted. We regret that this balanced and realistic text was not adopted owing to the negative vote of the United Kingdom.

The draft responded to the urgent humanitarian needs of the Syrian people. It renewed the cross-border mechanism for twelve months, retained the three authorized crossings, and at the same time reaffirmed the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and the temporary nature of the cross-border mechanism. It also contained necessary provisions to prevent the diversion of humanitarian assistance to terrorist groups and to expand cross-line deliveries in coordination with the Syrian authorities, in accordance with humanitarian principles.

We are concerned that the veto was cast not because the text failed to address humanitarian needs, but because some Council members sought to impose approaches that disregard the legitimate concerns of the Syrian Government and the realities on the ground. The humanitarian situation in Syria must not become hostage to political bargaining. The Russian Federation will continue to work for a balanced renewal of the cross-border mechanism and for the expansion of cross-line humanitarian deliveries, in full respect for Syria’s sovereignty and international humanitarian law.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom did not speak before the vote, but we wish to explain our vote. We take no pleasure in voting against this draft. The humanitarian needs in Syria are acute and the cross-border mechanism must be renewed. That is precisely why we could not support a text that falls short of what is required.

We welcome the twelve-month renewal and the retention of Bab al-Hawa, Bab al-Salam and Al Yarubiyah. But this draft omits Al-Ramtha, a crossing needed to reach civilians in southern Syria, and it retains language that risks subordinating cross-line deliveries to the consent of the Syrian authorities. Humanitarian access must be needs-based and consistent with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence. It cannot be made conditional on the approval of any party to the conflict.

The United Kingdom has used its veto with regret, but we could not support a draft that narrows humanitarian access and weakens the Council’s humanitarian intent. This was not a vote against the people of Syria. It was a vote against a flawed text that could not command the Council’s support and would not have delivered the principled humanitarian renewal that the situation demands. We remain committed to Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and we will continue to work for a robust, principled and effective humanitarian mechanism that reaches all Syrians in need.
